name: Devin
product: Autonomous cloud AI software engineer (plus Devin Desktop/CLI, formerly Windsurf) that plans, codes, tests and opens PRs from tickets.
free_tier: Yes (Free plan; no cloud agent on Free per tailkits)
starting_paid_price: Pro $20/month (Max $200/month; Teams $80/month base + $40 per seat)
latest_funding: Series E, over $2B at $48B valuation, announced 8 Sep 2026 (led by a16z and Accel); prior Series D $1B at $26B in May 2026
africa_evidence: A Luma event page for 'Build with Devin MeetUp Kampala #1' says Devin and Cognition are coming to Kampala, Uganda, with Devin credits for attendees, Cognition swag and a live Devin demo for students, engineers and founders.
payment_methods: Major credit and debit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link via Stripe; Klarna in some regions (docs.devin.ai/desktop/accounts/usage)
africa_use_case: Lagos and Nairobi startups with small teams could hand off backlog tickets to Devin Pro and pay the $20 plan plus usage from a naira or shilling wallet instead of a dollar card.
notes: Evidence for 'In Africa' is a single community-facing meetup page; the page does not name the organiser, so confirm it was run with Cognition. Docs ask users with unlisted payment methods to contact support, a natural opening for Cozzipay. privacy@cognition.ai and security@cognition.ai are the only published addresses found (privacy/security contacts, not sales). LinkedIn company slug 'cognition-ai-labs' appears in an official post URL but the company page itself was not seen.

name: Factory (Droids)
product: Droids: AI coding agents that plan, write, test and review code from a desktop app, CLI, SDK, IDEs, Slack and ticketing tools.
free_tier: Yes (Free BYO-inference tier added late 2026; not listed on all pricing snapshots)
starting_paid_price: Pro $20/month (Plus $100, Max $200; Teams $60/month + $40 per seat)
latest_funding: $200M at $5B valuation, Sep 2026 (total over $400M); Menlo Ventures also invested Oct 2026
africa_use_case: African dev agencies doing outsourced work for foreign clients could run Droids from the CLI on the $20 Pro plan to raise throughput without needing a dollar card.
notes: Enterprise-led (Nvidia, Adobe, EY customers) but has a cheap self-serve Pro plan. support@factory.ai published in Factory's Microsoft Marketplace listing; sales@factory.ai appears in Factory's public docs on GitHub. HQ San Francisco with a New York office.

name: Warp
product: Open-source agentic development environment built on a terminal, with a built-in Warp Agent, CLI agent and cloud agents (Warp Factories).
free_tier: Yes (Free plan; client open source under AGPL-3.0/MIT since Apr 2026)
starting_paid_price: Build $20/month ($18 annual) including $20 of agent usage; Max $200; Business $50/seat
latest_funding: Series B $50M, June 2023 (Sequoia); about $73M total. No newer round found
payment_methods: Card: purchases charge the team's saved payment method, which Warp's docs refer to as a card
africa_use_case: Backend and DevOps engineers in Nigeria and Kenya who live in the terminal could keep a Build plan and usage reloads funded from local currency.
notes: Do not confuse with Warp (HR/payroll startup) which raised a $60M Series B in June 2026. billing@warp.dev is published on Warp's plans and refunds doc page. Usage reloads and auto-reload suit Cozzipay's recurring/top-up flow.

name: OpenHands
product: Open-source (MIT) platform for AI coding agents that write code, run commands and open PRs, with self-hosted Teams and Enterprise tiers.
free_tier: Yes (open source, self-host with your own LLM key)
starting_paid_price: Teams $500/month including 10 users (+$50/seat); earlier cloud credit refills from $10
latest_funding: Series A $18.8M led by Madrona, Nov 2025 (about $23.8M total)
founders_or_ceo: Robert Brennan (CEO); Graham Neubig; Xingyao Wang
africa_use_case: A mid-size Nairobi fintech engineering team could self-host OpenHands Teams for governance and pay the monthly team fee locally.
notes: Paid entry point is a $500/month team plan, which limits self-serve African demand; most individual use is free OSS with BYO keys.

name: Jules
product: Asynchronous coding agent that clones a GitHub repo into a cloud VM and completes tasks, available on web, CLI and API.
free_tier: Yes (15 tasks per rolling 24 hours)
starting_paid_price: Bundled in Google AI Pro ($19.99/month in the US); Ultra tier higher
latest_funding: Part of Google (Alphabet)
africa_evidence: Jules Pro is sold only as a benefit of Google AI Pro. Google gives Google AI Pro free for 12 months to university students in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and Zimbabwe, and a report cites a Kenyan AI Pro price of KSh 3,700/month, but none of these sources mention Jules.
availability_in_africa: Google said Jules is available worldwide wherever the Gemini model is available (blog.google). Paid plans require a personal @gmail.com account.
payment_methods: Not found (Google AI plans are billed through Google One / Google Play)
africa_use_case: Nigerian developers on personal Gmail accounts could upgrade to Google AI Pro for higher Jules task limits.
notes: Borderline case. Jules docs tie Jules Pro to Google AI Pro, and Google AI Pro shows local pricing and an Africa student programme, so the parent should decide whether that chain counts. Google's checkout already has local-currency billing in Africa, so the Cozzipay pitch is weaker.

name: Cosine
product: AI coding agent (formerly Genie) running across CLI, VS Code, desktop and cloud; the company now also builds the Lumen Sovereign model for regulated UK/EU users.
free_tier: No (no free tier per review sources)
starting_paid_price: Hobby $20/month (Professional $200/month; add-on credits per 1M)
latest_funding: Seed; about $3.5M-$6M raised in total per third-party profiles (€2.2M round in Aug 2024); also UK Government-backed compute
africa_use_case: Small African teams maintaining legacy codebases could use the $20 Hobby plan for ticket-to-PR fixes.
notes: The 'Genie' name was retired in 2026. The company is pivoting toward UK sovereign AI and enterprise (BT, Lloyds, Vodafone coalition), so self-serve is a smaller focus. Pricing figures from third-party listings (Starter $19 also reported); cosine.sh/pricing did not show amounts in search.

name: Tembo
product: Control plane that runs background coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and others) across repos, tickets and team tools.
free_tier: Yes ($10 one-time allowance)
starting_paid_price: Pro $60/month (includes $60 usage, up to five users); Max $200/month
latest_funding: $14M Series A led by GreatPoint Ventures (July 2024); $20M raised in total
founders_or_ceo: Ry Walker (founder and CEO); co-founders Darren Baldwin, Benjamin Akar
africa_use_case: A five-person Lagos product team could share one Pro plan to run background agents on Jira or Linear tickets.
notes: Pivoted from managed Postgres to coding agents. HQ country inferred from US funding coverage; exact city not confirmed.

name: Goose
company: Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation); originally built by Block
product: Free open-source (Apache-2.0) local AI agent with CLI, desktop app and API that runs commands, edits files and orchestrates multi-step coding work.
free_tier: Yes (fully free, open source; no paid plan)
starting_paid_price: None (free; users pay their own model provider)
latest_funding: Part of Block originally; now a foundation project
africa_use_case: Cost-sensitive African developers can run Goose against local Ollama models, but there is no checkout for Cozzipay to serve.
notes: Donated by Block to the Agentic AI Foundation; no paid product, so it is a weak merchant prospect. Kept because it is still an active AI coding agent.

name: Gemini CLI
product: Open-source (Apache-2.0) terminal coding agent for Gemini models, now positioned for enterprise Code Assist and paid Gemini API/Vertex keys.
free_tier: Yes (open source; free Gemini API key tier with daily limits)
starting_paid_price: Paid Gemini API / Vertex AI usage or Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise; no individual subscription since June 2026
latest_funding: Part of Google (Alphabet)
africa_evidence: Google runs African programmes such as a Lagos Developers Space and free Google AI Pro for African students, but no source linked these to Gemini CLI.
payment_methods: Not found (Google Cloud billing for API/Vertex)
africa_use_case: Kenyan developers already on Google Cloud could use Gemini CLI with paid API keys billed through their Cloud account.
notes: Since 18 June 2026 Gemini CLI no longer serves Google AI Pro/Ultra or free Code Assist users, who were moved to Antigravity CLI; one source says Google stopped selling the Code Assist licences it relies on from 9 Oct 2026. Consider Antigravity CLI as the live Google prospect instead.

name: OpenCode
product: Open-source (MIT) AI coding agent for terminal, desktop and IDE that works with 200+ model providers, plus paid model plans (Go, Zen, Black).
free_tier: Yes (open source; free models available)
starting_paid_price: OpenCode Go $10/month; Zen pay-as-you-go; Black $200/month
latest_funding: Seed: SST raised about $1M after YC (2021); no newer round found
founders_or_ceo: Jay V (CEO); Frank Wang (CTO); Dax Raad; Adam Elmore
africa_use_case: Student and junior developers across Africa could subscribe to the $10 Go plan for open-weight models, a price point that suits mobile-money budgets.
notes: Very large user base (about 16M monthly developers and about 160,000 subscribers reported mid-2026), cheap entry plan and top-up model. Funding figure relates to SST era.

name: Crush
product: Open-source terminal coding agent with LSP context and MCP support that connects to 20+ model providers or Charm's own Hyper subscription.
free_tier: Yes (open source, bring your own keys)
starting_paid_price: Charm Hyper from $10/month (up to $200/month) or pay-as-you-go
latest_funding: Not found
africa_use_case: Go and backend developers in South Africa and Nigeria could pay for a $10 Hyper plan instead of juggling several foreign API accounts.
notes: Charm sunset its Mods tool in March 2026 to focus on Crush. Hyper pricing from one third-party listing only.

name: Mistral Code (now Mistral Vibe)
product: Vibe (formerly Le Chat plus Mistral Code) is Mistral's unified agent with a terminal coding agent (Vibe CLI), VS Code extension, web and desktop apps.
free_tier: Yes
starting_paid_price: Pro $14.99/month before tax (Team $24.99/user/month; student discount)
latest_funding: Series D €3B (about $3.5B) at about €21B ($24B) valuation, Sep 2026, led by Samsung Electronics
africa_evidence: Mistral signed a strategic AI partnership with Côte d'Ivoire's digital ministry in Aug 2026 and one with Morocco that produced Darija models, but neither source links them to Vibe or its coding agent.
africa_use_case: Francophone developers in Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal and Morocco could subscribe to Vibe Pro for a French-language coding agent priced below most US rivals.
notes: Mistral Code was folded into Vibe; Le Chat was renamed Vibe in 2026. Government ties in Côte d'Ivoire and Morocco make Francophone Africa a credible pitch angle.

name: Qwen Code
company: Alibaba (Qwen team / Alibaba Cloud Model Studio)
product: Open-source (Apache-2.0) terminal and IDE coding agent for Qwen models, usable with a Qwen subscription, Alibaba Coding Plan or any compatible API key.
free_tier: Yes (open source CLI; the free hosted OAuth tier closed on 15 Apr 2026)
starting_paid_price: Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan Pro $50/month; Qwen Plus/Pro subscription also unlocks Qwen Code (price not found)
latest_funding: Part of Alibaba Group
africa_use_case: Price-sensitive African teams could use the Coding Plan for low-cost Qwen, Kimi and GLM models inside Qwen Code.
notes: Free tier removal in April 2026 pushed users to paid plans. Alibaba's own checkout and its link to the Qwen consumer subscription were not confirmed.

name: GitLab Duo
product: GitLab Duo Agent Platform: AI agents across the DevSecOps lifecycle (coding, security remediation, pipelines) billed through GitLab Credits.
free_tier: No (included credits come with paid Premium/Ultimate seats)
starting_paid_price: GitLab Premium $29/user/month billed annually, including GitLab Credits
latest_funding: Public company (NASDAQ: GTLB)
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. GitLab runs a global reseller programme, but no African reseller or partner surfaced.
africa_use_case: African banks and telcos that self-host GitLab could add Duo credits for agentic security fixes and pay invoices in local currency.
notes: Mostly annual seat licences sold to organisations; less of a one-click self-serve fit. Included credits drop to 8 (Premium) and 16 (Ultimate) per user from 19 Nov 2026 for new customers.

name: Bito
product: AI code review agent for GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket PRs, IDE and CLI, plus a model router (Governor) for coding agents.
free_tier: No (14-day free trial, no card required)
starting_paid_price: Team $12/seat/month billed annually ($15 monthly)
latest_funding: Seed extension $5.7M led by Vela Partners, May 2025 ($8.8M total seed)
founders_or_ceo: Amar Goel and Anand Das (co-founders, previously PubMatic)
payment_methods: Stripe (card payments) per Bito billing security docs
africa_use_case: Small Nigerian and Kenyan engineering teams could add automated PR review at $12-15 per seat, a price that fits local budgets if they can pay without a dollar card.
notes: Founders' PubMatic background includes a large engineering base in India. Card-only Stripe checkout makes the Cozzipay pitch concrete.

name: Refact.ai
product: Open-source AI coding agent and assistant for VS Code and JetBrains with chat, autocomplete and self-hosted enterprise deployment.
free_tier: Yes (Free plan; open source)
starting_paid_price: Pro $10/month
latest_funding: Not found (one data provider says no external funding)
founders_or_ceo: Oleg Klimov (founder); co-founders Vlad Guber and Oleg Kiyashko
africa_use_case: Junior developers in Ghana or Kenya could upgrade to the $10 Pro plan for more agent usage inside VS Code.
notes: HQ per Crunchbase listing (London). Low price point but smaller brand.

name: Blackbox AI
product: Multi-agent coding platform and encrypted inference API routing 300+ models, used to dispatch coding agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini).
free_tier: Not found (conflicting: older reviews list a free tier; a Nov 2026 source says it is now enterprise-only)
starting_paid_price: Earlier 2026: Pro $10/month (credit-based); current site shows per-token billing against an annual enterprise commit
latest_funding: Not found (sources conflict: one lists $38.3M raised, another says no funding)
founders_or_ceo: Robert Rizk (CEO); Richard Rizk (CTO); Roger Rizk (COO)
africa_use_case: Blackbox has a large student user base; if self-serve plans still exist, African students could pay for Pro from mobile money.
notes: Business appears to be shifting to enterprise inference (annual commits, dedicated deployments), which weakens the self-serve pitch. Verify current self-serve plans before outreach.

name: Kimi Code
product: Kimi Code CLI (MIT-licensed) and coding service powered by Kimi K3 models, bundled with Kimi membership plans.
free_tier: Yes (CLI is free and open source; free Adagio chat plan has no coding quota)
starting_paid_price: Plus/Moderato $19/month ($15 annual) for coding; Pro $39, Max $99, Ultra $199
latest_funding: $3.5B at $35B valuation, July 2026; reported round at about $50B in Oct 2026
founders_or_ceo: Yang Zhilin (founder and CEO); co-founders Zhou Xinyu, Wu Yuxin
africa_evidence: No evidence found in searches. A Kenyan Substack post discusses Kimi K3 for Kenyan businesses, but that is commentary, not company presence.
payment_methods: Kimi API platform: bind a Visa, Mastercard or UnionPay card (min $1 deposit); API billing may offer online payment or bank transfer by region. Membership checkout methods not confirmed
africa_use_case: Cost-conscious African developers could use Kimi K3 through the $19 plan as a cheaper frontier-class coding model.
notes: Published addresses: membership@moonshot.ai (payment issues) and api-service@moonshot.ai. Card-binding requirement for API top-ups is a clear Cozzipay gap.

name: Codebuff
product: Open-source multi-agent terminal coding assistant and SDK; Freebuff is the ad-supported free version.
free_tier: Yes (Freebuff, ad-supported; open source Apache-2.0)
starting_paid_price: Credits at 1 cent each; subscriptions from $100/month
latest_funding: Y Combinator Fall 2024 (amount not found)
founders_or_ceo: James Grugett (founder and CEO); Brandon Chen (co-founder)
africa_use_case: African freelancers could buy small credit packs at 1 cent per credit for occasional heavy refactors instead of a monthly subscription.
notes: The company focus has shifted to free, ad-supported Freebuff (launched Feb 2026), so paid demand may be shrinking.

name: Amp
company: Amp Inc. (Amp Frontier Corporation), spun out of Sourcegraph
product: Terminal-first, multi-model coding agent with hosted cloud machines ('orbs') per thread, also usable in editors.
free_tier: Yes (Hobby: bring your own subscription or keys; Amp Free admissions were paused in Feb 2026)
starting_paid_price: Megawatt $20/month (students and teachers $10); pay-as-you-go credits from $5
latest_funding: Spun out of Sourcegraph as an independent company in Dec 2025; said to be profitable; no outside round found
africa_use_case: African computer science students could take the $10 student Megawatt plan, and working developers could top up $5 credit packs locally.
notes: SWAP: replaces Codegen (acquired by ClickUp; standalone service discontinued 9 Jan 2026).

name: Cline
product: Open-source (Apache-2.0) AI coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the command line, with an SDK and human approval for each action.
free_tier: Yes (open source, bring your own keys)
starting_paid_price: ClinePass $9.99/month; usage-billed Cline credits; Teams $20/user/month (first 10 seats free)
latest_funding: $32M combined seed and Series A led by Emergence Capital, July 2025
africa_use_case: VS Code users across Africa could buy the $9.99 ClinePass or top up Cline credits instead of opening several foreign API billing accounts.
notes: SWAP: replaces Plandex (Plandex Cloud wound down in Oct 2025; now self-hosted open source only, no paid product). Reports in Jan 2026 said OpenAI hired most of Cline's core team, but the company kept shipping through Oct 2026.

name: Kilo Code
company: Kilo Code (acquired by Anaconda, Inc., July 2026)
product: Open-source, model-agnostic coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, web and CLI with 500+ models at provider rates.
free_tier: Yes (open source extensions; pay-as-you-go usage)
starting_paid_price: Kilo Pass $19/month (also $49 and $199) with bonus credits; Teams $15/user/month
latest_funding: Acquired by Anaconda (Austin, Texas) in July 2026
africa_use_case: Data science and Python teams in South Africa and Nigeria already on Anaconda could add Kilo Pass credits for agentic coding.
notes: SWAP: replaces Ona (formerly Gitpod), which per Coder is now part of OpenAI; Ona Cloud closed on 31 Oct 2026 and the product is VPC/enterprise only. Kilo still operates as a product under Anaconda; Kilo Pass and pricing pages were live in Nov 2026. A tailkits review notes a 5% fee on credit purchases.
